1a.title: 1 in 3, aged 30–79
1a.caption: Most of us first hear about our blood pressure by accident — a clinic visit for something else, a pharmacy stop, a work check-up. It is common: about 1 in 3 Nigerian adults aged 30 to 79 (36%) has hypertension, and there is usually nothing to feel. Thirty seconds on the wrist is how you check on purpose. leiko.health

sources.name: WHO NCD Data Portal — Nigeria country profile
sources.figure: Quoted label, retrieved 2026-08-16: "Prevalence of hypertension among adults aged 30–79 years (age-standardized estimate) (%)" = 36%. Also on the page: raised blood pressure (SBP>=140 or DBP>=90), adults 30-79 = 32%.

1b.title: You can't measure BP from the wrist
1b.caption: Somebody has probably told you a wrist device is just guessing. Many are — they estimate from a light sensor. Leiko is different: a real cuff inflates on your wrist, holds, and measures — the same method as the cuff in a clinic. leiko.health

1c.title: Check on Papa
1c.caption: Every Sunday you ask Papa how he is, and every Sunday he says he is fine. One press on his wrist shows you the number behind “I'm fine” — wherever you are. A small way to check on him, often. leiko.health
